The reframing every lane arrived at independently

Our per-model quality is two to four points behind the field, and ensembling has been substituting for it. Forum thread 735304 (READ, verified by the orchestrator): single models at 224 px score 0.936 (single fold, small ResNet), 0.938 (single fold;
also #1 on the efficiency board, "as small a model as possible"), 0.934 → 0.942 (5-fold, 224 px).
We are at 0.926 with 22 members of one recipe.

The ensemble lane is closed by arithmetic, not by taste (lane 3, MEASURED): the gold return curve over random k-subsets of our 22 is flat past k ≈ 12, the marginal per extra member is +0.0001 to +0.0005, not one of the 22 has a resolved leave-one-out gain, and OOF's ranking of member value has no relationship to gold's (r = −0.08).
Five members are near-duplicates of their argmax twins (rho 0.990–0.996).
No 7th–9th fold and no recombination reaches 0.96, and the standing prohibition on both is confirmed with a number.

Defects in what is deployed right now (lane 2, REPRODUCED by reading the code)
src/tta.py:242 collapses the 2.5D packing. crop, bright and rot± rebuild the bag from channel 0 only and repeat it three times.

With --adjacent, channel 0 is the i−1 slice (dicom_io.py:539). 12 of the 22 deployed members are --adjacent and the kernel runs crop,bright, so 24 of 66 member-view forwards in the 0.926 submission run on a tensor no training sample ever had — three copies of the preceding slice.
smoke_test.py:2683 asserts the defect ("the three channels stay identical") because its fixture is non-adjacent.

The target side (lane 4, REPRODUCED)

The permitted α = 0.5 self-distillation target is resolvedly closer to expert truth than the teacher. On the 58 gold studies, 0.5·teacher + 0.5·deployed-22 scores 0.9217 against the teacher's 0.8976 and the model's 0.8987: +0.0233 [+0.0022, +0.0455] and +0.0241 [+0.0083, +0.0403], paired intervals excluding zero, stable across SWA-only, family-10 and rank pooling.
Reproduced exactly by the orchestrator from lane 4's appendix script.
Model and teacher correlate at only r = 0.455 across gold resamples — half-independent raters, which is the precondition for the blend to help.
Consequences: T035 is promoted back above the input-side levers (PLAN-0901 §5 C2 demoted it on an instrument argument that lane 3 also refutes, §5 below);
the 0.9545 "text-oracle ceiling" bounds report-derived labels, not the LB, and is one hardcoded string in eval_llm.py:56 that should be sourced or retired;
the deployed 22 has already closed 0.010–0.020 of all four "gap columns" and beats its teacher on Effusion resolvedly (0.948 vs 0.841).

Closed with reasons: co-teaching/noise-robust losses (targets are already soft posteriors), label smoothing (no-op), per-cell confidence weights from label metadata (the metadata does not exist), gold fine-tuning (0.9210 in-sample / 0.7342 nested precedent, and two public negatives), test-time recalibration (AUC is rank-only per column).
The measurement problem, restated with numbers (lane 3, MEASURED)

- The "transfer collapse" is mostly arithmetic. Spearman-rho deltas run 2.24× the AUC deltas on the same predictions, and compare_ckpts.py can only average the members that held a study out, so OOF's "22-member config" is a 4.4-member average per study — the steep part of the return curve.
The two factors turn 6.97× into 1.37× on 10→22.

The "teacher-agreement" reading survives only as a ~13 % component: scored against Sonnet, an independent labeler on the same 3,749 studies that never trained anything, 87 % of the 16→22 OOF gain survives.
- A better free instrument exists: OOF AUC (not rho) against the Sonnet labels, paired half-width ±0.0019, power 0.999 at +0.005.
Gold's paired band is ±0.0100 with power 0.165 at +0.005, so T037's B1 rule passes a true zero 16 % of the time and fails a true +0.005 half the time.
Gold stays a veto, and greedy selection on gold loses −0.0053 out of sample — Rule 4 is now empirical.
- Public-subset noise: one-member swaps have sd 0.0001–0.0003 (a displayed +0.001 is real);
a 10→22-sized nested step has paired band ~±0.006 (lane 4);
structurally distinct configs have sd 0.003–0.007.
Picking the best public score among ~40 distinct submissions manufactures ~+0.010 of worthless public gain.
The final selection rule must be written before the scores exist.
- Every rank/logit/weighting scheme measured on OOF is resolved-positive and −0.0002 to −0.0010 on gold — the ROADMAP ban on rank averaging stands.
- Every instrument here except gold measures report-agreement. The hidden truth is expert, image-derived.
The only route to a truth-anchored instrument at n ≫ 58 is an external expert-labeled set (T037-B2), now rules-permitted.

Where the lanes disagreed, and the resolution.
- Density: lane 1 says the frontier runs ~96 slices;
lane 2 says --adjacent closes 95 % of the coverage gap.
Both are right: the frontier's 96 comes from 6 slots × 16, i.e. from the second sequence family, not from density in one plane.
Slots first (lever 3), density last (lever 10).
- Resolution: lane 2 measures us 1.6× coarser than acquisition;
lane 1 finds 448 px does not beat 336 in a lesion probe.
The mm crop (lever 4) is the free half of the resolution lever and comes first;
384 px only behind it.
- Backbone: lane 2 keeps T025 alive on the optimizer-flags argument;
lanes 1 and 3 show capacity and diversity-by-correlation are both nulls.
Resolution: T025 runs as a diversity arm with the flags passed, ranked 7th, not as the capacity screen it was registered as.
- Cropping: lane 2 says tissue fills 99 % of rows so there is "no free crop";
lanes 1/5 say a 130 mm crop clips 0.5 % of series.
A 130 mm crop at a 160 mm median FOV trims ~19 % per side of the field, which is femoral/tibial shaft, not joint.
That is the frontier's bet;
the tripwire is the two labels that can sit there.
- Public noise: lane 3's 0.0001–0.0003 is for one-member swaps;
lane 4's ±0.006 is for a 10→22-sized step.
Rules use lane 4's bands.

Honest expectation

Summing the optimistic ends — self-distillation +0.010, second sequence family +0.010, mm crop +0.005, recipe +0.005, a diversity arm +0.005 — reaches 0.96 only if every lane pays at its optimistic end, and this log's record is that four of the last five mechanism-sound ideas came back null.
The realistic read is 0.940–0.948 on the public board, i.e. the current top 20 to top 50, plus a genuine shot at the efficiency prize.

What is different from every previous plan in this repo: the levers are the ones ~2,800 teams have already measured on this exact data, the instruments that misled the last three weeks are now priced, and the first two steps cost no training at all.

# RESEARCH-0902b — round 2: the single-model premise was wrong, and the levers got cheaper
Status: research complete 2026-09-02;

This amends [RESEARCH-0902](RESEARCH-0902-road-to-0960.md), it does not replace it: §1 corrects that document's central premise, §2 is a delta against its §6 ranked table, and nothing else in §6 moves.

The premise correction
RESEARCH-0902 §2 built its reframing on "single models at 224 px score 0.936, 0.938, 0.934 → 0.942".
Those figures come from forum thread 735304 and are unverified author claims;
lane 6 went looking for one with an artifact.

The verifiable public single model is 0.924, not 0.936. READ, the dreaddevelopment "Raptor" CoAtNet docstring: "0.924 on the public leaderboard using one model, with no ensembling and no test-time augmentation." Weights, inference script and training script are all public and CC0.

The 0.936 that is ID-anchored (submission 55802512) is a 35-checkpoint four-arm fusion, which its own author calls "now likely overfit to the public leaderboard" after "a user-driven fork-and-republish race [that] is not meaningful model development" (READ, lane 7 §6).
Our 22 at 0.926 is level with one public model — not two to four points behind a field of them.
The per-model-quality reframing stands, and the gap is ~0.024 — from one of our folds to their one model.
Arm C fold 0 scores gold 0.8793 (MEASURED, outputs/t028/armC_fold0.log) against the Raptor's 0.9054 on the same 58 (READ);
their gold→LB offset over two READ pairs is +0.019/+0.022, putting our fold near 0.89–0.90 (INFERRED).
The gold gap itself, 0.0261, is inside the ±0.036 tripwire and is not resolved — the direction rests on three independent LB pairs, never on a gold delta.
The last ~0.010 to the plateau is arm diversity, not member count. Their 0.936 is one 0.924 model plus ~35 checkpoints across four architecturally different arms;
ours is 22 of one recipe, on a curve lane 3 measured flat past k ≈ 12.
Labels are not the difference. MEASURED: data/csv/train.csv has 4,407 rows, exactly 58 with any label.
READ, the public training notebook's own header: it refuses to run without an LLM-built soft-label parquet the user supplies, the same construction as data/llm_labels.csv.
Lane 5's finding that our teacher (gold 0.8976) beats the best published LLM reader (0.881) stands.

Ordering. Full-data training is rank 1 by evidence and is deliberately gated behind S1 and S2. It forfeits the OOF instrument for its members — removing the held-out fold removes the split every rule here is written against — so it can only ever be judged by one submission.
Run it after the screens, so the full-data folds carry the winning recipe rather than being trained twice.

S1 and S2 rules, as lane 6 §4 wrote them. Each is one local fold against outputs/t028/armC_fold0, byte-identical except the named flags, same fold, same --seed 0 --split-seed 0, same 869-study corpus split.
- Adopt (build a family) if OOF corpus rho beats arm C by ≥ +0.012 with the paired 95 % interval excluding zero.
Kill if the paired delta is ≤ 0.000.
Unresolved in between: no family, no submission, record it — a second fold is not authorised by this rule.
Gold veto, every branch: abandon if gold macro-AUC < 0.8433 (0.8793 − 0.036).

The Raptor arm, and what is refused
Lane 7 §7's six rules, carried verbatim into [T044](../pm/tasks/T044-public-coatnet-member.md).
CC0-1.0 only, and nothing whose training code is not also public.
Fidelity gate before anything is scored: the reload must reproduce gold-58 macro AUC within ±0.010 of 0.9167 on our decode.
Four irreconcilable public figures exist (0.9054 / 0.9128 / 0.9167 / 0.9213), so none may be quoted as the target — hence the band.
Failure means a preprocessing bug, not a member.
Measure locally before submitting: score it over our 4,349 corpus, write its OOF, recompute the blend table with real numbers.

w = 0.20, fixed, never swept.
No per-label weights. A sweep is rule-constant tuning, refused in advance;
per-label weights are exactly what the plateau's own authors call "most likely to be public-leaderboard fitting rather than signal."

Mounting the 0.936 fusion notebook is refused, and not on taste.

It imports an author-admitted public-LB overfit — lane 5 measured that lineage going 0.936 → 0.935 twice on ID-anchored submissions when a better specialist was added — and its DINOv2/RadImageNet arms train in private Kaggle kernels, so §2.8's obligation to deliver training code cannot be satisfied from public material. The Raptor is the opposite case: weights, inference script, training script and preprocessing recipe are all public under CC0, and a winner's reproduction description would be honest and complete.

One prerequisite the six rules do not cover. Joining a foreign model's predictions to ours needs a per-column percentile-rank join — the two share no calibration, and a probability mean would let the more confident branch dominate a rank-only metric.

Lane 7 §3.2 flags that this touches the standing ban on rank averaging and says "it is not for a lane report to declare the ban narrowed." T044 is blocked on an operator note narrowing that ban to the cross-calibration case. For the record, the ban's textual home is T026's STOP verdict and RESEARCH-0902 §5, not ROADMAP § "Explicitly not worth doing", where a grep finds nothing.

fastMRI+ beats MRNet because it is image-derived and covers 7 columns against 2.
Its defect: the annotated fastMRI knee set is coronal only (READ), so our three-plane model would score with two of three plane slots padded.
That threatens instrument validity, and it is falsifiable for free.
Gate 0 runs before the licence step. Score deployed-22 and T024-10 on ~1,000 of our own studies with the sagittal and axial slots masked, against the Sonnet labels (paired band ±0.0019 at corpus n).

Recommendation — a pre-registered final-selection rule
Not a submission, not a GPU hour, not a code change.
A rule, written now, judged at the close.

Never leave the final two to Kaggle's automatic selection. Not because its criterion is known to be bad — it is not documented on any page read — but because it is undocumented, unauditable, and certainly not reading the instruments that separate our candidates.

Slot 1 — best by instrument, not by leaderboard. Among submissions whose public scores are within the nested-comparison noise of the best, take the one that leads on the corpus rho / OOF-AUC-vs-Sonnet pair, with gold as a veto.
On today's evidence slot 1 is 55954418, the fixed-TTA 22, and it is chosen over 55896111 on a resolved +0.0124 rho despite an identical public score.

Slot 2 — a structural hedge, not the runner-up. The second slot should be the most architecturally different config that is not disqualified, so the two selections do not fail together on the same private draw.
It should not be a near-copy of slot 1, because two nested configs give one bet twice.
The efficiency track is selected separately and does not consume these two — confirm this against the efficiency-prize eligibility text before the close;
lane 11 owns that question.
Re-evaluate the rule, not the picks, whenever a new instrument lands. The rule is what is pre-registered;
which submission satisfies it is allowed to change as evidence arrives.

Registered as a task rather than executed here, because the close is 2026-10-22 and the right time to make the pick is late — but the right time to fix the rule is now, while no candidate exists to bias it.
